name: AD844
type: Current-feedback op-amp, single, with TZ node
tagline: Its ~50 Ω current-feedback input and exposed TZ node make it a DIY favourite for open-loop DAC I/V stages.

lineage.note: Sole source on ADI's complementary bipolar process. Barrie Gilbert design credit unconfirmed.

part_numbers.note: PDIP-8, −40 to +85 °C, RoHS; the usual DIY part. Widely stocked.
Non-RoHS PDIP-8; obsolete per DigiKey, which names AD844ANZ as direct substitute.
CERDIP-8, −40 to +85 °C; B grade has 150 µV max offset.
SOIC-16W, 0 to +70 °C; only SMD option, different pinout from DIP-8.
Non-RoHS SOIC-16W; reportedly in PDN 10_0081 Rev. B.
CERDIP-8, −55 to +125 °C; /883B is MIL-screened. Separate AD844S page.

reputation.summary: A DAC DIY favourite for I/V: DAC current enters the low-impedance inverting input and the TZ node feeds a buffer, usually without global feedback. The long diyAudio thread 'Using the AD844 as an I/V' calls it the 'best opamp based I/V so far by a long way' and rates it above the OPA627. These are forum opinions, not measurements.
typical_uses: Open-loop I/V for current-output DACs, buffered by OPA627
2–3 paralleled per channel for lower I/V impedance
caveats: Feedback resistor sets bandwidth; a capacitor directly in the feedback path invites oscillation.
Open-loop TZ use leaves gain, linearity and DC offset uncorrected by feedback.
6.5 mA per part adds up when several are paralleled.
Only SMD package is SOIC-16W; no 8-lead SOIC for drop-in swaps.
Praise comes from subjective forum listening.

counterfeit_notes: No AD844-specific counterfeit reports, but remarked eBay/AliExpress op-amps are well documented (Hackaday, Super-Freq). Buy from authorized distributors; be wary of loose 'AD844AN/JN' DIPs sold as new, since current production is AD844ANZ.

claims_confirmed: Current ADI datasheet is Rev. G, 20 pages (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/data.html?di=351709, https://analog.com/en/products/ad844.html).
Farnell 13931.pdf holds the old-format REV. C datasheet (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/13931.pdf).
AllDatasheet 48466 is a 12-page REV. C copy (https://www.alldatasheet.com/html-pdf/48466/AD/AD844/19/1/AD844.html).
60 MHz (G=−1), 33 MHz (G=−10), 2000 V/µs, 20 MHz FPBW (20 V p-p, 500 Ω), 150 µV, 6.5 mA, 80 mA (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad844.pdf).
Settles to 0.1% in 100 ns, nearly independent of gain; TZ transcapacitance 4.5 pF typ (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/77786.pdf).
Ordering codes ANZ, AQ, BQ, JRZ-16, JRZ-16-REEL7, SQ, SQ/883B (https://analog.com/en/products/ad844.html, https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/analog-devices-inc/AD844BQ/621197).
AD844JR-16 listed in PDN 10_0081 Rev. B, medium confidence (https://www.analog.com/media/en/pcn/ADI_PDN_10_0081_Rev_B_Form.pdf).
A separate AD844S product page exists (https://www.analog.com/en/products/ad844s.html).
Rev. G revision table: Rev. G 5/2017 (Figure 32, Ordering Guide), Rev. F 2/09, Rev. E 1/03, Rev. D 11/01: https://www-cce.cldnet.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD844.pdf
Input voltage noise 2 nV/√Hz at f ≥ 1 kHz; open-loop transresistance 3.0 MΩ typ (VOUT ±10 V, 500 Ω): https://www.komponenten.es.aau.dk/fileadmin/komponenten/Data_Sheet/Linear/AD844.pdf
Operates from ±4.5 V to ±18 V supplies: https://www.analog.com/en/products/ad844.html
AD844AN obsolete at DigiKey, AD844ANZ named direct substitute: https://www.digikey.bg/en/products/detail/analog-devices-inc/AD844AN/611708
